parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A pundit's forecast that a team packed with English players will do well.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what is expected to happen, a straightforward synonym of prediction.

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word stupid

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: Someone calls a dim-witted fool smug for being pleased with himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with themselves, a plain synonym.

parts.note: to rob is to take what belongs to someone else

explanation.surface: An instruction to adopt a stray bird, taking it into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a familiar garden songbird with a red breast, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Comfortable seat extended round back of bureau

indicators.note: round says the longer word goes about the single letter

parts.note: something extended has been made longer

indicators.note: back of picks out the final letter of the word bureau

explanation.surface: An office armchair has been stretched out around the rear of a writing desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining chair or couch for relaxing, a kind of comfortable seat.

parts.note: reads like a question about duration, but 'time' is slang for a prison term, and the longest a court can impose is one lasting until death

explanation.surface: An abstract question about the greatest stretch of time imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing time means serving in prison, and the longest prison term is one for the whole of the offender's remaining years.

parts.note: an ass is a stupid person
the ending -ess marks a female, as in lioness or actress

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to judge a woman as foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up word: adding the feminine ending -ESS to ASS gives a 'female fool'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or appraise, so it means judge as a verb.

clue.text: Wild trip many miles away within Somali borders

indicators.note: within says the distant piece sits inside the two border letters
the borders of the word Somali are its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: afar means at a great distance

explanation.surface: A trip into the wild, far off inside the borders of Somalia.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition to see wild animals, so it is a trip into the wild.

clue.text: Letters moved with list, as supporting structure

indicators.note: moved says the letters of the word Letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: a table is a list of figures or facts set out in rows

explanation.surface: Letters rearranged alongside a list, perhaps in a typesetter's layout.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a board laid on trestles, a temporary framework holding things up, so it is a supporting structure.

indicators.note: on places the stance next after the drink in the across entry

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
a pose is an affected attitude put on for show

explanation.surface: Someone presumes a drinker is striking an affected attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to take something as true without proof, a synonym of assume.

clue.text: Season not kicking off for Bury

indicators.note: not kicking off means the season's word loses its opening letter

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A football club called Bury not starting its season.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is an English football club, which suits 'kicking off', but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, a formal synonym of bury.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words learner driver

explanation.surface: A socially awkward geek is taking driving lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, a synonym of geek.

clue.text: Old park warden ending in steamy greenhouse for fruit

parts.note: a ranger looks after a park or forest

indicators.note: ending in picks out the final letter of the word steamy

explanation.surface: An elderly park keeper ends up in a steamy greenhouse growing fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass-roofed building originally used for growing citrus trees, a greenhouse for fruit.

definitions.meaning: ... here is the adjective meaning hard and unyielding

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for solidness and a noun for a commercial company.

indicators.note: docking an animal means cutting its tail short

parts.note: the rabbit is the animal

indicators.note: tail is the last letter of the animal

explanation.surface: A Jewish official docking an animal's tail, perhaps in a ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docking' is the cutting signal: RABBIT loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader, so an official of the faith.

indicators.note: around says the word for change goes about the little word at

parts.note: a conversion is a change from one form to another

explanation.surface: A spoken suggestion to rearrange things during a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversation is an informal exchange of words, a synonym of talk as a noun.

clue.text: Plate left in possession of hoarder

indicators.note: in possession of says the hoarder holds the single letter inside

parts.note: a saver puts things by rather than spending them

explanation.surface: A plate left behind ends up in a hoarder's collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A salver is a flat serving tray, often of silver, a kind of plate.

clue.text: Mother keeps representative in the shade

indicators.note: keeps says the mother word holds the representative inside it

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
an agent acts on someone's behalf

explanation.surface: A mother keeps her agent waiting in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the shade' looks like a place to rest, but 'shade' means a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, and a shade is a particular tone of a colour.

clue.text: Plant requiring drainage in a storm

indicators.note: in a storm suggests the letters of drainage are tossed into disorder

explanation.surface: A plant needs good drainage to survive during a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a fragrant white-flowered evergreen shrub, an example of a plant.

clue.text: European sandwiches unfortunately from New Zealand, perhaps?

indicators.note: sandwiches says the European holds the regretful word in its middle

parts.note: an Austrian is a European by nationality
alas is an exclamation of regret

explanation.surface: A European laments having to make sandwiches, which comes from New Zealand?
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealand lies in Australasia, so something from there is one example of being of that region.

clue.text: Skilled worker going after power is prejudiced

indicators.note: going after places the worker behind the letter for power

parts.note: an artisan is a skilled craftsperson

explanation.surface: A craftsman chasing power is biased.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisan describes someone strongly biased in favour of one side, a synonym of prejudiced.

definitions.meaning: in football, the defender who plays behind the back line to clear any danger

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sweeping brush and the football defender who mops up behind the back line.

clue.text: Shooting star that's remote, breaking up

indicators.note: breaking up says the letters of remote fall apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A shooting star far away disintegrates in the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is the popular name for a meteor, a space rock burning up in the atmosphere.

parts.note: something lit up is clearly visible
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A spotlit man shows how nimble he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and flexible in movement, a synonym of agile.

indicators.note: leader going AWOL means the first letter of the word for crazy goes missing

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Crazed soldiers whose commander has deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large organised body of soldiers, so it stands for soldiers collectively.
